name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: No polling or expert ratings on the race
model.rationale: The R+19 district, Meuser's incumbency and 2-to-1 fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing him near 96% all point to a safe Republican hold; the Democratic challenger has no visible polling or outside support to justify moving off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing Wallace within single digits would warrant a shift toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dan Meuser seeks another term in a northeastern Pennsylvania district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of about R+19. He has raised roughly $1.9 million and holds a cash advantage over Democrat Rachel Wallace, who has raised about $700,000. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets price Meuser's chances near 96 percent.

Wallace faces an uphill climb in a seat Republicans have held comfortably, and the modest Democratic national environment is not enough to close a double-digit structural gap. The forecast calls for Meuser to win by a wide margin, with the race rated Safe Republican.
